rationale: ACPT-04 performance budget — LOCKED. Numeric thresholds (cold + warm wall-clock per fixture/profile/engine/phase) derived via D6-01 measure-first methodology: the executor ran `npm run perf` (harness across worst-case fixtures × desktop + throttled-mobile-chromium profiles × 3 engines), computed p95 from 5 samples per cell (120 total), proposed thresholds at measured p95 + 25% headroom (rounded up to clean numbers), and the USER APPROVED them before locking. Mirrors how Phase 3 derived the calibration tolerance empirically (D3-02). The 25% headroom is baked INTO the wallClockMs values (toleranceBound.headroomPct=0 so the gate fires strictly when fresh p95 > wallClockMs — no double-counting). D6-03: the fallback scrolling commit shares the warm budget — one gate. Fallback was not triggered by any worst-case fixture across viewports 320-1280px (the engine paginates all successfully); the architectural argument (Plan 04-05 + 04-08: fallback = same measurement engine + always-mounted ArticleBody → commit work ≤ warm repagination) confirms the warm p95 bounds fallback. Worst cases: cold = webkit (611-647ms across all fixtures; webkit's fonts.ready + JS exec is substantially slower); warm = throttled-mobile chromium (503-509ms) and webkit (456-523ms), both coalescer-debounce-bound and fixture-independent. p95WallClockMs + sampleCount are the latest measured values (refreshed each passing run); wallClockMs is the LOCKED threshold. RE-BASELINE 2026-09-26 (issue #101, USER-APPROVED — D6-01/D6-04): chromium desktop list-reference/technical-post COLD 60/70 → 100ms. The repair evidence (webkit cold p95 838-948 → 618-670ms; eager article graph 131 → 125 src modules) restored every load-bound cell, but these two cells kept firing (63-77ms draws vs 60/70 budgets) because their harness samples are same-document fragment navigations that read the stale DEV hook — they measure dev-server protocol latency under 3-worker contention (observed 5-77ms; a REAL cold load of the same fixtures measures ~500ms via page.reload), not reader-facing pagination. At lock time the same frame carried only ~25% headroom (locked p95s 48/48). A/B with the deferred snapshot arm routing-blocked moved swap timing ~8ms (median 449 → 457ms), ruling out app-code interference; no module shedding can move a protocol-latency measurement. The 100ms ceiling keeps the locked same-frame semantics (strict when fresh p95 exceeds it) with headroom over the observed contention tail; every other cell's threshold is byte-unchanged.
